chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).
Regarding His saying, the Blessed and Exalted:
And He answers those who believe and do righteous deeds, and increases them from His grace.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the believer who supplicates for his brother in his absence, so the angel says to him,

key_terms.بِحُبِّكَ إِيَّاهُ: Due to your love for him
key_terms.بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ: In his absence / behind his back

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for praying for someone else in their absence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanism of divine response to intercessory supplication, emphasizing that Allah grants the supplicant a reward equal to the merit of the one prayed for, rooted in the bond of love (hubb). It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual efficacy of praying for others in their absence, linking personal devotion directly to communal solidarity and divine generosity.
